In mathlib we have that the addition of two commuting topologically nilpotent elements is topologically nilpotent in the following lemma

import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.TopologicallyNilpotent

variable {R : Type*} [TopologicalSpace R] [Ring R]

/-- If `a` and `b` are topologically nilpotent and commute,
  then `a + b` is topologically nilpotent. -/
theorem add_of_commute_test  [IsLinearTopology R R] {a b : R}
    (ha : IsTopologicallyNilpotent a) (hb : IsTopologicallyNilpotent b) (h : Commute a b) :
    IsTopologicallyNilpotent (a + b) := by
 sorry

However, in my work I am trying to formalise power bounded elements following Wedhorn, and here we can show that the set of power bounded elements of a nonarchimedean ring are a ring (prop 5.30). With this I then want to define the residue field of power bounded quotient topologically nilpotent.

Therefore, I would quite like to have a similar statement as above but with Nonarchimedean R instead of IsLinearTopology R R (which I have sorry free in my own repo).

The important fact is that nonarchimedean rings do not necessarily have the linear topology e.g. the p-adic numbers, and furthermore I do not believe these two statements can be unified. IsLinearTopology R R and ContinuousConstVAdd R R should imply TopologicalRing R - detailed in implementation notes of Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.LinearTopology, which together means we could state the following instance.

instance (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]:
    NonarchimedeanRing A where
  is_nonarchimedean U hU := by
    obtain ⟨J, hJ, hJU⟩ := (IsLinearTopology.hasBasis_open_ideal (R := A)).mem_iff.mp hU
    exact ⟨⟨J.toAddSubgroup, hJ⟩, hJU⟩

But I do not think IsLinearTopology R Ralone is enough to imply NonarchimedeanRing R.

Thus, it seems like the new NonarchimedeanRing R lemma may need to be included alongside the existing lemma. My question is whether this seems an acceptable duplication of work - or if there is something else we could do?
@Antoine Chambert-Loir as the linear topology and topologically nilpotent files are yours
If S is the ring of power bounded elements, or of elements of norm <= 1, wouldn't you have LinearTopology S R ? (Just a guess)

docs#IsLinearTopology should definitely imply docs#NonarchimedeanRing, unless I'm mssing something obvious. In fact, a linearly topologized module is a nonarchimedean additive group because a basis of submodules is in particular a basis of subgroups.
Sorry, I read too fast and misunderstood your issue.

To be clear, you are claiming that factoring the proof of docs#IsTopologicallyNilpotent.add through NonarchimedeanRing would add hypotheses, right ? What are they ? For example, I'm pretty sure we can get rid of the commutativity assumption in your instance.

I am claiming that we could have the following

/-- If `a` and `b` are topologically nilpotent and commute,
  then `a + b` is topologically nilpotent. -/
theorem add_of_commute ‘  [NonarchimedeanRing R R] {a b : R}
    (ha : IsTopologicallyNilpotent a) (hb : IsTopologicallyNilpotent b) (h : Commute a b) :
    IsTopologicallyNilpotent (a + b) := by
 sorry

which is completely separate and this and the existing lemma cannot imply eachother. I am then concerned that it could cause a lot of duplication of code if we wanted both

I think no one will complain about adding [IsTopologicalRing R] to the assumptions of docs#IsTopologicallyNilpotent.add_of_commute; the notion of linearly topologized rings is only ever useful for topological rings (if you can't translate stuff to zero then it's useless, and if you can then you are in fact a topological ring). Does this answer your question, or am I still misunderstanding something?
If we were to add the IsTopologicalRing R then docs#IsTopologicallyNilpotent.add_of_commute would be exact by the new lemma with NonarchimedeanRing and the above instance.
Which would suggest a refactor if we are happy to lose the case of having addition when we only have IsLinearTopology R.
Yes sorry this is exactly what I meant (but I wrote it in a strange way)

OK. It is my impression that NonarchimedeanRing R is very close to IsLinearTopology Int R, and that this latter assumption should be enough to imply the topological nilpotence of the sum of two topologically nilpotent elements which commute. Can one add an instance of NonarchimedeanRing once one has a IsLinearTopology S R for adequate S and R?
Unfortunately this can’t be a general instance because Lean can’t infer what the ring S might be. But we can have a general theorem and then specific instances for S = R or S = Int
Note that this should be generalized to : a linearly topologized module over any ring is a nonarchimedean group
I have a PR #40013 with my suggested changes following these discussions. Feel free to have a look and see if there is anything you would suggest.

@William Coram I will have a closer look a bit later. There are interesting things in your PR; in particular, I claim that your IsBounded (generalized to a topological module over a topological ring) should replace our docs#Bornology.IsVonNBounded (but let's leave this for later).

Let me just note that neither Antoine nor myself will be enthusiastic to review Claude-generated code.

No worries. The PR is on about the third iteration of full rewriting (by me) after Claude generated proofs based on the Wedhorn reference I mentioned earlier - the label is just there for transparency.
